annotation.title_clean: Advisory Guidelines on Use of Personal Data in Generative AI
annotation.title_en: Advisory Guidelines on Use of Personal Data in Generative AI
annotation.summary_en: Singapore PDPC advisory guidelines explaining how the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 applies to generative AI across development, deployment and post-deployment. They cover the publicly available exception, consent and notification, stakeholder roles, and access and correction requests. They are non-binding and concern no physical systems.
key_provisions_or_claims: Web-scraped personal data behind digital barriers requires assessment of public availability, documented in a DPIA or written record.
General notifications are insufficient for large-scale generative AI training on user data; AI-specific notifications are required.
Model providers, system providers and deployers can be organisations or data intermediaries with Protection and Retention obligations.
System deployers bear primary responsibility for PDPA compliance and should review safeguards for agentic AI.
Access and correction obligations apply to generative AI data, with best practices such as data provenance and output filters.
